Staff must confirm the traveler identity, the animal details, and the route file before any movement is accepted for service. The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions and resolves exceptions that fall outside routine handling, while desk staff preserve consistent care for every traveler and pet.

The boarding document required for this process is FM-597. Clear communication with the traveler is essential, and staff must avoid unnecessary discussion that distracts from the record check.

Jonah Meyer and Zain Ali are examples of travelers who depend on accurate service handling, but every traveler receives the same careful attention. Companion Animal Travel Desk Boarding Rules

This section sets the standard for handling animal travel requests with care, consistency, and clear service.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk serves passengers traveling with companion animals across Aurelia Skyways routes, and every case is handled as a shared service duty. Staff must confirm the travel record, carrier details, and customer instructions before any animal is accepted for movement. The boarding form FM-597 is the required document for boarding and must be complete before the journey is approved. If any required item is missing, the desk does not proceed until the record is corrected and the traveler is guided through the next step with calm, respectful language.

The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions and resolves exceptions when a route, animal type, or document review creates uncertainty. Staff are expected to keep their wording simple, avoid rushed promises, and treat the animal and traveler as one service unit. When a customer presents a pet such as Sadie for travel, the desk checks identification, container condition, and the traveler note against the service record. Any sign of stress, unsafe handling, or conflicting instructions requires immediate pause and review before acceptance continues. The desk does not shift responsibility to another unit without clear handoff, and it does not accept an animal if the required standards are not met.

Passenger privacy and animal welfare remain equal priorities. Information about the traveler, pet, and trip is shared only with staff who need it to complete service. The desk keeps communication courteous and factual, especially when explaining limits, delays, or follow-up actions. If a traveler like Jonah Meyer or Zain Ali requests clarification, staff provide it in direct language and confirm the next service step without offering guesses. Records must be kept accurate, legible, and current so that the journey can be managed without avoidable confusion.

The desk also keeps a careful watch on the condition of the carrier, the readiness of the animal, and the fit between the animal's needs and the planned route. If an issue appears after initial review, staff stop the process and bring the matter to the senior coordinator at once. The goal is always the same: safe handling, steady communication, and dependable service from check-in through departure.

For any exception, uncertainty, or service concern, contact the senior coordinator or the Companion Animal Travel Desk.

This section sets out the minimum handling and booking rules for birds accepted by Aurelia Skyways, and it is written to reduce avoidable error in our service.

I regret that any ambiguity has ever reached the desk, so these rules must be followed exactly. The fee for a bird is $145, and staff shall record it in the booking notes before carriage is confirmed. The longest side of the crate for bird transport is 60 cm, and no crate that exceeds that limit shall be accepted. A crate must remain secure, clean, and well ventilated, and staff shall check that the latch closes firmly without strain. Calm and humane handling is required at every stage, with slow movements, low voices, and no rough repositioning of the animal or container. The senior coordinator oversees daily service decisions, and front-line staff shall refer any doubt about fitness for travel, crate condition, or acceptance at once rather than improvising a response.

When a traveler presents a bird, the agent shall confirm the crate before payment is finalized and shall explain the transport conditions in plain language. If the crate is damaged, unsafe, or too large, the booking shall not proceed until the issue is corrected. If the bird is sensitive to noise or handling, staff shall limit unnecessary contact and keep the animal in a quiet holding area until transfer to the cabin team. The cabin team monitors animals during flight and shall receive complete booking notes, including the approved crate details and any handling instructions entered by the desk. No employee shall promise an exception that has not been approved through the senior coordinator, and no service note shall be left incomplete when the animal is accepted.

Quality checks have shown that clear records prevent delay and reduce stress for both traveler and animal. For that reason, the Companion Animal Travel Desk must verify the fee entry, crate limit, and handling notes before the reservation is closed. If a traveler arrives with a bird named Mia, Andre Nguyen, or Khalil Costa, the same rules apply without preference or deviation.
